newsitem.title: USA: Bergen Brunswig cancel Ivax deal, files suit.
newsitem.headline: Bergen Brunswig cancel Ivax deal, files suit.

text.p: Bergen Brunswig Corp. filed a lawsuit Friday against drug maker IVAX Corp., one day after Bergen called off its $1.6 billion takeover of IVAX Corp.
A spokeswoman for the company declined to comment on the details of the lawsuit, which was filed under seal in New York.
However, the company said earlier the lawsuit charged IVAX with breaching its merger pact.
On Thursday, Bergen said it terminated the merger. The deal would have been the nation's first combination of a major drug wholesaler and a large maker of generic drugs.
Industry analysts said the surprise decision could force Ivax to sell assets and take other restructuring measures.

"From the standpoint of contrarians or bottom fishers, IVAX has a lot (of positives). The company is getting its fair share of NDA (new drug application) approvals, so the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and IVAX are in good compliance, which is very valuable," Gruntal & Co analyst David Saks said.
"Over time, with better management and internal controls, it will likely turn around, but I don't know when the inflection point will be," said Saks, who rates the stock a neutral.
Bergen, based in Orange, Calif., said while it was terminating its agreement with IVAX, it would continue to pursue a strategy aimed at managing supply channel costs.

"Notwithstanding the termination of the IVAX agreement, we will continue to pursue our strategy, recognizing the valuable role that generics play," said Donald Roden, Bergen's president and chief executive officer.
A Bergen spokeswoman said she could not comment on precisely how the merger agreement had been breached because the matter was going into litigation.
"It involves things that have been occurring over the past few months," she said.

The Bergen-IVAX deal was announced in November, simultaneous with IVAX's announcement of its 1996 third-quarter earnings, results that included a net loss of $178.7 million, or $1.47 per share, after $118 million in restructuring and write-down charges.
Three months earlier, IVAX said it was in technical default of its revolving credit facility, forcing the company to seek a waiver.
IVAX's blamed the setbacks partly on customer inventory buildup related to the introduction in 1996 and 1995 of an unusually large number of U.S. generic drugs.
For all of 1996, IVAX lost $160.8 million, or $1.33 per share, on $1.15 billion in revenues vs. a 1995 profit of $114.8 million, or 96 cents per shar,e on $1.26 billion in revenues.

But IVAX significantly exceeded Wall Street earnings estimates for 1996's fourth quarter, posting a loss of 2 cents per share vs. the Zack's Investment Services consensus view of a 22-cent-per-share loss.

Hemant Shah, pharmaceutical analyst at HKS & Co, said, "If you read between the lines of IVAX's press release (on the Bergen deal), it says it and its advisers implemented certain strategies in anticipation of the deal potentially not going through. That could be a reason for Bergen perceiving there was a breach in the agreement."

"IVAX now has to restructure. They will have to divest assets. The company is a collection of many assets, like a chemical business, a diagnostics business, while the European assets are very valuable," Shah said.
IVAX said it was prepared to proceed independently.

"Recognizing the possibility that the Bergen merger might not be approved or completed, we developed, together with our advisers, a number of contingency strategies geared toward the success of an independent IVAX, and look forward to announcing and implementing those strategies in the near term," IVAX Chairman Phillip Frost said.

An IVAX spokesman told Reuters the company could not comment or speculate about Bergen's allegations because it had not yet been served with the complaint. "We don't see any sound basis for their unilateral termination," he said.
The spokesman said IVAX had already fashioned contingency strategies, which it would announce shortly, but he declined to reveal the specifics of those strategies.
IVAX stock dropped $1.625 to $10.75 on the American Stock Exchange on Friday, while Bergen gained 12.5 cents to $31.625 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
